text:
maria: heads-up — we're onboarding a new Private deployment and the customer asked what minimal GCP KMS perms their SA needs. also they want guidance on envelope rotation and where to push audit logs. any quick checklist?

ajay: +1. root question: will the Redwood control plane run in customer's project or are we impersonating a cross-project SA? that changes the bindings.

maria: customer will host KMS in their project and we'll impersonate a workload/service account in that project via short-lived creds. so we don't need owner-level perms.

ajay: ok. minimal bindings i've used: grant the service account roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter at the cryptoKey level (not keyring), and roles/cloudkms.viewer on the keyring if they need to list. avoid granting admin.

lucas: for envelope encryption pattern: we store DEKs locally (or in our datastore) but encrypted by the customer's KMS key. workflow: generate DEK, encrypt data with DEK, then encrypt DEK with KMS (encrypt API). rotate by generating new DEK and re-wrapping existing ciphertext with new DEK or re-encrypting DEKs with new KMS key version.

maria: can someone paste the gcloud one-liner for the binding? will share in the onboarding doc.

ajay: sure — example (customer-run):

```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding my-cmk \
  --location=global \
  --keyring=redwood-keyring \
  --member=serviceAccount:redwood-priv-sa@customer-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
```

ajay: if they insist on least privilege, attach to the specific cryptoKey name. avoid granting to the entire project.

carol: audit logging note: enable DATA_ACCESS audit logs for Cloud KMS in the customer's project and create a logsink to their security/logging project or to our secure collector if contract allows. filter example for sink: `resource.type=\"kms_keyring\" OR protoPayload.serviceName=\"cloudkms.googleapis.com\"` — but suggest they include `protoPayload.methodName:\"Encrypt\" OR protoPayload.methodName:\"Decrypt\"` to get crypto ops.

kevin: one gotcha from support: if you rely on key version rotation, make sure your code detects key version metadata and retries with the new version; otherwise decrypt will fail when key version is disabled. add exponential retry and clear DEK cache on 403s from KMS.

lucas: for rotation at scale we recommend two options: (1) rotate KMS key versions and re-wrap DEKs (cheap) or (2) create a new KMS key and re-encrypt DEKs with the new key (safer audit trail). both require a rewrap job. here's a tiny Python pseudocode for rewrap loop:

```python
for row in db.select_all_encrypted_deks():
    dek = kms.decrypt(row.encrypted_dek)
    new_wrapped = kms.encrypt(new_key, dek)
    db.update(row.id, new_wrapped)
```

kevin: also log rewrap jobs to SIEM and emit metrics: rewrap_success, rewrap_fail, rewrap_lag.

maria: ops question — should we ask customers to give a dedicated keyring per Redwood tenant? pros/cons?

ajay: pros: easier ACL scoping + simpler audit filtering. cons: more objects to manage. if they have many tenants, key naming conventions and automation help. recommend a single keyring && per-tenant crypto keys (one cryptoKey per tenant).

carol: security checklist for onboarding (short):
- confirm SA identity and project
- grant roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter to SA on cryptoKey
- enable DATA_ACCESS audit logs for KMS and add sink
- set a rotation schedule (e.g., 90 days) and define rewrap runbook
- ensure monitoring + alerts on KMS permission errors

maria: perfect — i'll paste this into the private-deploy onboarding doc and ping infra to add the gcloud snippet. @ajay can you own adding the rewrap example to infra-runbooks?

ajay: yep i can. i'll draft a short runbook with the gcloud, sample IAM bindings, and a rewrap job template.

kms-bot: automated reminder — see internal/crypto/rotation-policy doc for Redwood defaults. next review date scheduled in 90d. :bell:

maria: thanks all. i'll follow up with the customer-specific checklist and share when ready. :thumbsup:
